questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This probes ability to implement tenant-scoped observability using a sidecar pattern, ensuring isolation of telemetry data and correct sink routing in a CNF gateway.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant-scoped telemetry and OpenTelemetry/Prometheus format
- Sidecar pattern for non-intrusive metrics augmentation
- Prometheus remote_write configuration per-tenant
- ConfigMaps for sink endpoints and TENANT_ID propagation
- RBAC, InitContainer for bootstrap, minimal namespace scoping

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal sidecar and main gateway manifest (snipped for brevity)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf/gateway:latest
      - name: telemetry-sidecar
        image: telemetry-sidecar:latest
        env:
        - name: TENANT_ID
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.labels['tenant_id']
        - name: REMOTE_WRITE_URL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: tenant-sinks
              key: sink_url
```

```yaml
# ConfigMap providing per-tenant sink URL
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tenant-sinks
data:
  sink_url: https://tenant-a-sink.example.com/api/v1/write
```

```yaml
# One-namespace test manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate or revoke sinks without downtime?
- How would you monitor for mislabelled metrics and alert on sink failures?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical traffic shaping, per-tenant configuration, and end-to-end validation in CNF gateways. It favors deterministic routing to avoid flapping and shows how to wire a ConfigMap-driven control plane into a sidecar.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant canary rollout
- Deterministic routing via hashing
- Namespace-scoped ConfigMap as control plane

## Code Example
```javascript
function shouldCanary(tenantID, path, canaryEnabled, percent) {
  if (!canaryEnabled) return false;
  const h = hash(tenantID + path) // 32-bit
  return (h % 100) < percent;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor rollout progress and rollback if issues arise?
- How would you handle multi-namespace deployments with shared upstreams?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design per-tenant controls using Kubernetes primitives and sidecar patterns.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant state with token bucket
- Namespace ConfigMap watch / refresh
- Sidecar deployment partnering with main gateway
- Fallback defaults and safe testing in one namespace

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenantRateLimit
  namespace: cnf-system
data:
  tenants.json: |-
    {
      "tenants": {"tenantA": 100, "tenantB": 50},
      "defaultRPS": 20
    }
```

```yaml
# sidecar snippet: mount ConfigMap and read /etc/cnf/tenants.json
volumeMounts:
  - name: tenant-rates
    mountPath: /etc/cnf
volumes:
  - name: tenant-rates
    configMap:
      name: cnf-tenantRateLimit
```

```yaml
# one-namespace manifest (test-tenant)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: test-tenant
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: cnf/gateway:latest
        - name: rate-limit-sidecar
          image: cnf/sidecar-rate-limit:latest
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tenant-rates
              mountPath: /etc/cnf
      volumes:
        - name: tenant-rates
          configMap:
            name: cnf-tenantRateLimit
```

## Diagram
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Ingress] --> B[RateLimiter Sidecar]
  B --> C[Gateway Backend]
```
